# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: Fixes a crash in the MessagePack source generator and analyzer when a [MessagePackObject] type has a member whose type is a closed generic struct from another assembly. In TypeCollector, two places read `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly; they now use null-safe lookups (line 985 through a new helper at 1434, line 1077 with `FirstOrDefault()`). Separately, every analyzer diagnostic now passes through a new filter (239, 1444-1450). The filter silently drops any diagnostic whose location is not a source tree in the current compilation. Three new tests build the defining code into a real metadata-only assembly. They assert no diagnostics and that the resolver is generated. README and MsgPack004.md gain a paragraph describing the new suppression policy.
story.why: Metadata symbols have no syntax references, so indexing `[0]` throws. The MemberNeedsKey diagnostic at old line 1076 is built unconditionally, so it crashes even in the generator, where no diagnostics are reported. That stops the resolver from being generated, which is the core harm in the issue.
touches_beyond_requirement: A global diagnostic filter (TypeCollector.cs 239, 1444-1450) that drops every analyzer diagnostic located outside the current compilation's syntax trees, including those with Location.None. This is a policy change, not only a crash fix.
README.md section 'Generic types from referenced assemblies' (1639-1643).
story.confidence_overview: High that line 1077 was a real crash site and is now safe. Medium that the tests would fail without the fix: the unkeyed-member test clearly reaches line 1077, but the diff does not show which path the all-keyed struct and record-struct tests hit. The issue names three indexing sites (735, 1009, 1101 in 3.1.8). Only two edits are visible, and the diff does not show whether the third exists or is fixed. Medium-low that the new diagnostic filter has no unintended suppression for source types.

refusals.what: Analyzer now suppresses all diagnostics whose location is outside the current compilation, including Location.None.
refusals.why: This changes user-visible analyzer behavior; some previously reported warnings or errors may disappear. That is a product decision, not a crash fix.

refusals.what: README and MsgPack004.md documentation committing to a policy that referenced-assembly diagnostics belong to the defining project.
refusals.why: Neither the documentation nor the policy was requested by the requirement; the owner should decide whether to adopt it publicly.

findings.description: The filter drops every analyzer diagnostic whose location is not in source, including Location.None. Any existing diagnostic for a source-declared type whose location helper returns null (e.g. GetParameterListLocation, GetIdentifierLocation) was previously reported at Location.None and is now silently suppressed. This could hide real user errors beyond the metadata case. No test covers that it doesn't.

Problems in referenced-assembly types are now never surfaced in the consumer. This assumes the defining assembly ran the analyzer, which may be false for NuGet packages built without MessagePack's analyzer. A real misconfiguration could then go unreported anywhere.

The issue lists three `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (including one near line 735 in 3.1.8); this diff edits two. If a third unconditional `[0]` access remains in GetObjectInfo, other shapes of metadata generic struct could still crash. That cannot be confirmed from the visible hunks.

It is not demonstrated that ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference and ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference fail without the fix. Their members are all keyed, so they may not reach line 1077, and the diff does not show which crash path they exercise.

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic whose location is Location.None (since Location.None.IsInSource is false), which silently suppresses valid diagnostics for types declared in the current compilation whenever a location helper returns null. For example, GetPropertyIdentifierLocation (line 1434) casts the property syntax as PropertyDeclarationSyntax, returning null for in-source positional record or record struct primary-constructor properties (ParameterSyntax, e.g. [property: Key((string)null!)]) and indexers (IndexerDeclarationSyntax), causing BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull (line 985) to be created with Location.None and silently dropped; the same happens for diagnostics using GetParameterListLocation (line 1454) when method is null or implicitly declared.

In the true branch of the same unconditional ternary fixed on line 1077, Diagnostic.Create(MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AOTDerivedKeyAttribute, derivedKeyAttribute.GetSyntax(this.cancellationToken).GetLocation()) still assumes syntax exists. If a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly has any public or private member annotated with a custom attribute derived from KeyAttribute (with suppressSourceGeneration not true), AttributeData.ApplicationSyntaxReference is null for metadata symbols, throwing NullReferenceException on both the generator path (CS8785, omitting the resolver) and the analyzer path (AD0001).

out_of_scope.description: New documentation section describing that referenced-assembly type diagnostics are reported only by the defining project.
New section documenting the same suppression policy for MsgPack004.
The global ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter (239, 1444-1450) changes diagnostic reporting for all diagnostics, not just the crashing indexing sites.
